# exercise { #wdm.exercise }

`exercise`

Estimating exercise energy expenditure from a logged lifting session.

The `exercise_kcal` column in the observations schema (see ``data/schema.md``)
is optional, and left blank it is absorbed into the estimated maintenance
parameter along with everything else unmodeled -- harmless if your training
volume is roughly stable, but a real gap if you want expenditure to track a
session that actually happened.

This module estimates it from a set-by-set lifting log using the standard
MET (metabolic equivalent of task) method:

$$
\text{kcal} = \text{MET} \times W_{\text{kg}} \times \text{hours}
$$

with MET values from the Compendium of Physical Activities
(Ainsworth et al.): resistance training at vigorous effort is coded 6.0,
light-to-moderate effort 3.5. This is a rule-of-thumb estimate, not a
measurement -- treat it with the same suspicion the report gives wearable
calorie counters. It answers "roughly how much," not "exactly how much."

**Session duration is estimated, not logged**, since the tracker records sets
and reps rather than a stopwatch. Per set: working time is reps times a
seconds-per-rep figure parsed from the tempo column when present (a
dash-separated tempo like ``4-2-2-0`` is standard notation for
eccentric/pause/concentric/pause in seconds, and the four numbers sum to a
per-rep duration), plus a fixed rest period that depends on how demanding the
movement is. Isometric holds (no reps logged) use a duration parsed from the
notes column when it matches an ``M:SS`` pattern, and a flat default
otherwise.

**Exercises are classified compound / isolation / core from the tracker's own
Muscle Guide sheet**, via its "Movement Pattern" column, rather than a
separately maintained lookup table. This is a deliberate choice: it means the
classification updates automatically if you add exercises to the Muscle
Guide, instead of silently falling back to a default the moment your workout
log outgrows a hardcoded list.

### classify_movement { #wdm.exercise.classify_movement }

```python
exercise.classify_movement(movement_pattern)
```

Map a Muscle Guide "Movement Pattern" string to compound / isolation / core.

Isometric core work ("Isometric Core") and unlabelled core-only movements
both fall under "core" rather than "isolation": both are lower-MET,
non-loaded-to-failure work, and lumping them keeps the category count
small enough that each one's MET assumption is defensible rather than a
guess per exercise.

### estimate_session_kcal { #wdm.exercise.estimate_session_kcal }

```python
exercise.estimate_session_kcal(log, weight_lb)
```

Estimate exercise_kcal for each calendar date present in a loaded tracker.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name      | Type         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                          | Default    |
|-----------|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| log       | pd.DataFrame | Output of `load_tracker`, or any frame with the same columns (Date, category, Reps, Tempo, Notes).                                                                                             | _required_ |
| weight_lb | float        | Body weight to use in the MET formula. This is *your* weight, not the dumbbell load logged per set -- the two are easy to conflate since both are in pounds. Pull it from your most recent weigh-in. | _required_ |

### load_tracker { #wdm.exercise.load_tracker }

```python
exercise.load_tracker(path)
```

Read the workout tracker's log sheets, joined against its Muscle Guide.

Expects the three-sheet layout produced by the tracker template: "Upper"
and "Lower" log sheets with columns (Date, Session, Exercise, Set #,
Weight (lb/hand), Reps, Tempo, Equipment Cap?, Notes), and a "Muscle
Guide" sheet keyed by (Session, Exercise) with a "Movement Pattern"
column.

Returns a long-format frame, one row per logged set, with a `category`
column already attached. Title and instruction rows, and any trailing
free-text notes rows, are dropped by requiring a parseable date.

An exercise with no matching Muscle Guide entry -- new, or logged under a
slightly different name than the Muscle Guide uses -- classifies here as
"compound" via `classify_movement`'s fallback, silently. This
function does not surface that; call `unmatched_exercises` on the
same path to check, since a fallback that never announces itself is easy
to carry for months without noticing.

### repeat_session_kcal { #wdm.exercise.repeat_session_kcal }

```python
exercise.repeat_session_kcal(log, session, as_of, weight_lb)
```

Estimate a session's kcal by reusing its most recently logged instance.

Built for a tracker used as a standing routine reference rather than a
live diary: a session gets logged once in full, and then simply repeated
-- same exercises, same weights, same reps -- until the routine changes,
with no new dated row added each time it recurs. There is then no row for
"today" to read directly. This takes the most recently logged occurrence
of `session`, re-dates a copy of it to `as_of`, and estimates from that --
which is exactly correct as long as the routine has not changed since that
entry, since the estimate depends only on the sets logged, not on which
calendar day they are dated.

If the routine *has* changed since the last logged instance -- different
weights, added or dropped exercises -- this will estimate the old
session, not today's. There is no way to detect that from the file alone;
log a fresh dated block when you actually change something.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                    | Description                                                                                                                                                                          |
|--------|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | (estimate, source_date) | The estimate re-dated to `as_of`, and the date it was copied from -- the caller should say so, rather than presenting a copied estimate as if it were read directly off today's log. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type       | Description                                                                              |
|--------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | ValueError | If no row in the log matches `session` (comparison is case- and whitespace-insensitive). |

```python
exercise.set_duration_seconds(row)
```

### unmatched_exercises { #wdm.exercise.unmatched_exercises }

```python
exercise.unmatched_exercises(path)
```

Distinct (Session, Exercise) pairs logged with no Muscle Guide entry.

The join in `load_tracker` is exact string matching, deliberately --
fuzzy matching an exercise name would silently paper over a real typo
just as easily as a real rename. The cost of exactness is that a mismatch
produces no error, only the quiet "compound" fallback, so this exists to
make that visible: run it whenever you add an exercise, since "compound"
(MET 6.0) and "isolation" (MET 3.5) are a real difference in the
resulting estimate, not a rounding error.

Returns pairs sorted for stable output, empty if everything matched.
